record_notes.DCP-LETT-1212: Wednesday within December 1848–1849 range. Schoolroom permission note known, Nash appointment prospective. Drawing reportedly sent but explicitly not received. Son had called twice unsuccessfully; microscope discussion Thursday or Friday depends on health. Missed Adams invitation, meteor paper thanked without explicit complete reading. Do not sequence this letter before 1210 solely from drawing absence versus drawings receipt; identity of the objects is unproved. Nash and Adams identifications in apparatus remain tentative.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1122: Monday assigned October 4, 1847; cover names Charles but salutation/body address Mary Lyell. Bergen label does not establish locality; Darwin explicitly marks it unknown. Specimen return promised, not completed. Charles note missing, Coal Saurian versus fish uncertain. Enclosed Chambers letter explicitly unlocated, and cannot be preserved October 5 incoming 1124. Hypothetical equal terraces, possible cooked coincidence, and sea/ice-lake alternatives retain uncertainty; survey funding proposed. Miller reading ongoing, later October 6 completion log not current state. Picture already hung, unlike prospective returns and publication.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1266: Wednesday night assigned October 24, 1849 from later Hancock letter. Requests translation of one page and title, language uncertain to Darwin; Lovén known by reputation, address not yet known. Does not already understand the requested page. Returns borrowed Footsteps and has ordered own copy, not received it. Supports denudation hypothesis from St Jago observations; later December 19 Lyell paper is future. Accepted 1262 later says Lady Lyell translated title and copied paper read, but actual incoming translation letter/text is absent.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1244: June 7, supplied 1849, Malvern. Earlier hurried printing-error note missing. Requests conspicuous correction or two-sheet reprint before dispatch, asks copies distributed; none proves remedy completed. P3 has literal duplicated/garbled Reader clause, confirmed in retained raw source, requiring explicit rendition review instead of silent repair. Later bibliography describes variant corrected and possibly uncorrected copies, not current Darwin knowledge.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1245: June 12, supplied 1849. Thanks missing Murray note and returns copies for correction. Asks whether reader/compositor will be fined and conditionally offers money; neither fine nor gift is established. Silence would be interpreted by Darwin as no charge to workman, not independent evidence. Corrected copies expected before month end and proof inspection offered conditionally. Claimed absence of errors except transposition is his contemporary assessment, not a modern verification.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1152: February 4, supplied 1848. Dinner invitation for Saturday 12 through Monday, attendance still partly uncertain: Bell unanswered and Owen hoped/believed. Raw MathML is one quarter before seven, about 6:45, not fourteen minutes or hours. Train 4:45 and two-horse fly for four are prospective travel advice. South America map requested; d’Orbigny comparison and whether Bone already used it unresolved. Later February 13 Ramsay diary confirms a visit retrospectively, not at invitation time. No Ramsay incoming answer survives.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1168: April 7, supplied 1848. Asks Ramsay to establish disputed Moel Tryfan height; Darwin cannot recall authority for own lower figure. Footnote compares Trimmer 1000, Darwin 1192, cited Murchison 1692, and later paper 1392 feet. None is an incoming answer or current resolved measurement. April 19 presentation is future; keep explicit uncertainty and unknown reply.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1335: Monday 27 assigned August 1849 by narrow mourning border and calendar, with alternatives November 1848 and May 1850 discussed and rejected editorially. Declines missing Ransome invitation because health requires regularity, has written Maguire. Summary claims December 1850 Henslow inauguration, inconsistent with assigned date and footnote suggesting portrait-publication dinner in 1849. Preserve unresolved event identity; later portrait sitting not current attendance. No Ransome input survives.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1261: October 25, supplied 1849. Requests subscription entry of one pound for Bishop portrait. Later account-book payment January 2, 1850 is one pound one shilling, not the same amount or proof of current completed payment. Bishop could be Stanley or Hinds according to apparatus; do not resolve by name guess. No preserved request letter.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1070F: Collective British Museum memorial, not individual Darwin prose despite single sender in XML. Darwin is thirtieth of 57 signatories according to apparatus. March 10, 1847 is presentation date, not proved drafting, signature or individual reading day. Advocates stronger natural-history management while explicitly opposing physical separation from other departments. Later royal commission, trustee changes and Kensington transfer are editorial outcomes, not current statements. No conversational incoming prompt.

Requests royal inquiry; 1850 commissions and later reforms not current outcomes. Joint text excluded from individual Darwin voice regardless of support by signature.

record_notes.DCP-LETT-1262: Accepted full primary reading reused with matched source and provenance hashes. October 29 OR 30, 1849. Alcippe specimens arrived safely but only cursory glance; fuller dissection deferred until generic descriptions finished and Hancock paper obtained. Received sketches identify Australian Ibla and provisional Machairis celata, later renamed; names and provisional classification must not be harmonized. Alder copy of Lovén paper now read, Lady Lyell translated title; asks academy location, unreadable host name and Alcippe etymology. Previously supposed familiar organism now recognized as new family/order, with original description considered short. Lithotrya model evolves: cup stays fixed, larva may enter cavity or bore chemically; Hancock cavity observations cause doubt. Raw MathML quarter inch, and small tiered cup diagram read. Existing statements are hypotheses and reports, not modern biological facts. Missing Hancock letter, sketches and copied paper text preclude direct prompt.
